name: Medad
title: One of the seventy elders who prophesied in the camp
summary: Medad was one of the seventy elders chosen to receive God's Spirit along with Moses. He and Eldad became known because they prophesied inside the camp instead of at the tabernacle, which caused controversy. Moses defended them and expressed a wish that all the Lord's people were prophets.

keyEvents.title: Chosen among the seventy elders
keyEvents.description: Medad was chosen as one of the seventy elders in Israel to share the burden of the people with Moses, after God commanded Moses to gather them.

keyEvents.title: God's Spirit rests on Medad
keyEvents.description: The Lord took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and placed it on the seventy elders, including Medad, so that they prophesied.

keyEvents.title: Prophesied inside the camp
keyEvents.description: Medad and Eldad had remained in the camp and prophesied there instead of going out to the Tent of Meeting like the other elders.

keyEvents.title: A young man reports to Moses
keyEvents.description: A young man ran and told Moses that Eldad and Medad were prophesying inside the camp, which caused unrest among some of the people.

keyEvents.title: Joshua asks Moses to stop them
keyEvents.description: Joshua, Moses' servant, asked Moses to forbid Eldad and Medad from prophesying, but Moses rejected this and defended their prophetic work.

keyEvents.title: Moses' answer about the prophetic gift
keyEvents.description: Moses answered Joshua with the famous statement: "Would that all the Lord's people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his Spirit on them!" This showed Moses' humility and desire for the outpouring of the Spirit.
